Fernando Pérez Calvillo (b. 1350, Tarazona) was a prominent entrepreneur and business leader of the Medieval period, active in Tarazona. He played a crucial role in shaping the economic and cultural landscape of the region during the 14th century.

As a key figure associated with the Tarazona merchant class, Calvillo was deeply involved in the textile industry, which was a significant contributor to the region's wealth. His business acumen and strategic partnerships helped to establish Tarazona as a major hub for trade and commerce in the Iberian Peninsula.

Calvillo's entrepreneurial achievements had a lasting impact on the region, contributing to the growth of Tarazona's population and economy. His legacy can still be seen in the city's historic architecture and cultural institutions.

Fernando Pérez Calvillo's story is a testament to the resilience and adaptability of the human spirit in the face of adversity, a reminder that even the most seemingly insignificant individuals can leave a lasting mark on the course of history.
